hints.title: Greedy Denomination Subtraction
hints.text: Roman numerals represent values using thirteen distinct additive and subtractive symbols. How can greedily subtracting the largest available denomination convert an integer?

hints.title: Descending Symbol Greedy Invariant
hints.text: Always choosing the largest symbol value less than or equal to remaining num guarantees the shortest valid Roman numeral representation.

hints.title: Ordered Pair Division and Appending Procedure
hints.text: List the 13 value-symbol pairs in descending order from 1000 down to 1. For each pair, while num is greater than or equal to value, append the symbol to the output and subtract value from num. Return accumulated string.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(1) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Analyzing digits individually with branching conditional ladders is error-prone and verbose.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Greedy deduction against thirteen ordered denominations terminates in at most 15 steps with O(1) auxiliary memory.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should explicitly include the 6 subtractive values (900, 400, 90, 40, 9, 4) in the lookup list to simplify code.
